reason: Full source arguments inspected: J. S. Milne v3.08, Ch. 5 Lemma 5.2 p.86; W. A. Stein, Algebraic Number Theory, section 8.1 Prop. 8.1.4 p.89. Strategy: if u is a unit with inverse v in O_K then Nm(u)Nm(v)=Nm(uv)=1 with both factors in Z, hence Nm(u)=+-1; conversely for |Nm(u)|=1 fix one embedding sigma_0 and put beta=product over sigma != sigma_0 of sigma(u), so u beta=+-1 and beta is a product of conjugates of an algebraic integer, hence an algebraic integer in K, i.e. in O_K, making u invertible. The argument itself introduces no Choice use and the item makes no standalone ZF claim; the converse direction is the one the unit theorem consumes and never passes through a norm being a unit in a larger ring.
